rules.statement: When a caller-supplied key reference or resource identifier names a host the server will call, accept only hosts under an operator-configurable allow-list of domain suffixes, and check it in both the validation path and the call path before any network request.
rules.why: Without an allow-list, a tenant can point the server at internal or attacker-controlled HTTPS endpoints (SSRF), and parts of the response can come back in error text.
rules.check: Look for caller- or tenant-supplied URLs, key IDs or vault URIs that are only syntax-checked (e.g. any dotted HTTPS host) before the server sends requests to them.

rules.statement: Reject an input longer than its persisted column's maximum length during validation, before any expensive remote call, using a constant shared with the entity's column configuration.
rules.why: Otherwise an oversized value costs a remote round trip and then fails at the store with a 500 where the caller should get a 400.
rules.check: Look for string inputs that are stored in length-limited columns but are validated only by format, or whose length limit is a separate literal from the column's.

rules.statement: Give each persisted column its own max-length constant named for that column instead of reusing a constant named for another column.
rules.why: Changing the other column's limit would silently resize this one too.
rules.check: Look for `HasMaxLength` or `[MaxLength]` on a property that uses a constant named for a different property.

rules.statement: Index the columns that a periodic or background query filters on, unless the table is documented as small by design.
rules.why: Without the index, each pass scans the whole table, which grows with usage.
rules.check: Look for new scheduled or polling queries whose WHERE columns have no matching index in the entity configuration or migration.

rules.statement: When a cache load guards its success path against a concurrent eviction or invalidation, apply the same guard before recording a failure.
rules.why: Otherwise a stale load that started before an eviction can record a failure after the eviction cleared it, and refuse requests for the whole retry interval.
rules.check: Compare the success and failure paths of a cache load: the failure path should check the same eviction counter or version before it writes.

rules.statement: Decide a derived fact once, where its data is read, and return it in the method's result instead of flipping a mutable state object deep in a call chain or recomputing it elsewhere.
rules.why: When the fact is decided in several places, a later change to its definition can miss one of them.
rules.check: Look for a mutable holder object passed into helpers to set a flag, or the same condition recomputed in a caller that a callee already decided.

rules.statement: Don't make a sequence of remote round trips (such as one KMS unwrap per row) while holding a per-key lock on the request path; limit the work to what the request needs, or move it outside the lock or to a background service.
rules.why: The first request waits N round trips, and concurrent requests for the same key queue behind it.
rules.check: Look for loops of awaited remote calls inside a held SemaphoreSlim or lock on a request path.

rules.statement: Enforce a domain invariant, such as which owners may perform an operation, in the domain service or manager and have the HTTP handler only map its exception to a status code; don't enforce it only in the endpoint handler.
rules.why: Another caller of the service would otherwise bypass the check.
rules.check: Look for authorization or eligibility checks that exist only in an endpoint handler while the service method it calls accepts any input.

rules.statement: Don't declare a private constant that duplicates a shared bound (such as a timeout) that already exists in a referenced layer; use the shared one.
rules.why: The two values can drift apart.
rules.check: Look for new private timeout or limit constants with the same value and purpose as an existing shared constant.

rules.statement: Read the clock once per event or record and use that value for every field derived from the time, such as a UUIDv7 id and the event timestamp.
rules.why: Separate reads can give the fields different times.
rules.check: Look for several `TimeProvider.GetUtcNow()` calls while building one object.

rules.statement: Don't give a public constructor, including an exception constructor, an optional defaulted parameter; expose the optional value as a nullable `init` property instead.
rules.why: Adding another optional input later breaks binary compatibility.
rules.check: Look for `= null` or other default values on parameters of public constructors in shipped packages.

rules.statement: When you edit an XML doc comment or Markdown paragraph, rewrap it to the file's line width (120 columns) and remove stray extra spaces.
rules.why: Edited lines that overflow or carry stray spacing break the file's layout, and Markdown lint may flag them.
rules.check: Look for edited comment or Markdown lines past 120 columns, or with runs of spaces inside a sentence.

rules.statement: Leave a blank line between a Markdown list or paragraph and the heading that follows it.
rules.why: Running content straight into a heading breaks the file's layout and may be flagged by lint.
rules.check: Look for a `#` heading line directly after a bullet or text line with no blank line between them.

rules.statement: Give a new shared UI component a Storybook story covering its main states (default, submitting, error, edge cases), as its sibling components have.
rules.why: Without one, its states can't be checked visually in isolation.
rules.check: Look for a new component in a shared UI package with no matching `.stories.tsx` file.

rules.statement: Don't report a cache or loader that fails closed on every load failure, without telling outages from revocations, when its remarks document this as deliberate.
rules.why: A component that can't tell an outage from a revocation must never serve material it couldn't validate again, so blanket fail-closed with a retry interval is a deliberate security choice.
rules.check: Before reporting, read the class remarks and the related ADR for a documented fail-closed decision.

rules.statement: Don't ask code behind a provider-neutral store abstraction to catch a typed unique-violation exception when the abstraction has none; detecting a duplicate by reading back the existing row after a failed insert, and rethrowing the original exception when no row exists, is correct.
rules.why: If a row exists, the insert could never have succeeded, so reporting a conflict is right whatever the store's exception was.
rules.check: Before reporting, check whether the store abstraction exposes a typed duplicate or concurrency exception, and whether the catch rethrows when no conflicting row is found.

rules.statement: In a test project, don't ask a unit test to replace a mocked event publisher with a recording event handler: unit tests assert what the subject hands to the publisher, and integration tests assert the recorded events through a recording handler.
rules.why: A true unit test isolates its subject from the event pipeline.
rules.check: Before reporting, check whether the test is a unit test of one class and whether an integration test already covers the recorded events.

rules.statement: In a test project, don't report `null!` when it passes a deliberate null to the code under test in an argument-validation test; the test conventions allow it there.
rules.why: The test conventions make `null!` the one allowed use of the null-forgiving operator in tests, for argument-validation tests only.
rules.check: Before reporting, check whether the `null!` is an argument to the subject in a test of its null-argument handling.

rules.statement: In a test project, don't report private nested fake or stub types inside the one test file or test helper that needs them; the no-nested-types rule is for production code, and the test conventions place them there.
rules.why: The test conventions say a fake that one test file needs goes in that file as a private nested type.
rules.check: Before reporting, check that the nested type is private and used only by its containing test file or helper.
